www.headerRoot: .uhf-header (UHF: brand, contextual nav + dropdowns, All Microsoft mega menu, search, me control, optional cart)
www.homeFlavour: a www nav doc WITHOUT a site-logo link (brand section has only the Microsoft link) renders .uhf-header.hp-header (index archetype: single 54px mobile row, product links, cart)

bing.headerRoot: .common-nav (sticky explore.microsoft.com nav: logos, Features/More popups, search expand, drawer < 811px)

support.headerRoot: .uhf-header.uhf-header-category (support.microsoft.com UHF category header + sign-in teaching callout)

chrome.selection: Page metadata `nav` (and `footer`). scripts.js maps a nav path ending in nav-bing / nav-support to that variant (else www) BEFORE first paint and sets <html class="chrome-<variant>">; metadata `chrome` (www|bing|support) overrides the mapping. The header/footer blocks render the variant template and MOVE the authored nodes of the nav/footer document into it.

breakpoints.policy: source steps, per variant (DESIGN.json extensions.breakpoints has no `target` set, so breakpoint-lint skips)

fonts.policy: Segoe UI is licensed: referenced from Microsoft's CDN (c.s-microsoft.com/static/fonts/segoe-ui/west-european/*/latest.woff2) exactly as the prototypes do, never rehosted. One font sheet per variant, loaded by scripts.js loadFonts(): styles/fonts.css (www: family SegoeUI, local('Segoe UI') first), styles/fonts-bing.css (family "Segoe UI" 300/350/400/600/700), styles/fonts-support.css ("Segoe UI" + "Segoe UI Semibold/Bold/Light/Semilight" + MWF-MDL2 icon font from www.microsoft.com/mwf).

stacks.www: --ms-font: "Segoe UI", SegoeUI, "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

styles.styles.css: tokens for all three variants, www base (MWF reboot + type ramp) scoped with :where() to zero specificity, bing/support page bases under :where(.chrome-x), utility canon (.container, .cta, .btn, .link-group, .card), EDS section model (default-content-wrapper = variant container)
styles.perArchetype: section/module styling lives in the archetype blocks, never in styles/
